ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by

aeneas: Aenēās, -ae (m.) — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Venus and Anchises (nom. sg.)

genus: genus, generis (n.) — race, family, birth, kind (nom./acc. sg.)

hinc: hinc (adv.) — from here, hence; from this
hoc: hic, haec, hoc — this (n. nom./acc. sg.; m./n. abl. sg.)
hominum: homō, hominis (m.) — human being, man (gen. pl.)
huic: hic, haec, hoc — this; huic, to/for this (dat. sg., all genders)
hunc: hic, haec, hoc — this; hunc, this man (m. acc. sg.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
illa: ille, illa, illud — that; she, that woman (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)

italiam: Ītalia, -ae (f.) — Italy (acc. sg.; first syllable long in verse)

iura: iūs, iūris (n.) — law, right, justice (acc. pl.)
laborem: labor, labōris (m.) — toil, hardship, trouble (acc. sg.)
lacrimans: lacrimō, -āre — to weep, shed tears (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
magno: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
manus: manus, -ūs (f.) — hand; handiwork (acc. pl.; also nom./gen. sg., nom./voc. pl.)
media: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
medios: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (m. acc. pl.)
mortalia: mortālis, -e — mortal; mortālia (n. pl.), human affairs (n. nom./acc. pl.)
multa: multus, -a, -um — much, many; multa (n. pl.) as noun, many things (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor
neque: neque (nec) — and not, nor; neque enim, for indeed… not
nos: ego, meī — I; nōs, we, us (nom./acc. pl.)
nunc: nunc (adv.) — now, at present; nunc… nunc, now… now
omnia: omnis, -e — all, every; omnia, all things, everything (n. nom./acc. pl.)
omnis: omnis, -e — all, every (acc. pl., = omnēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
operumque: opus, operis (n.) — work, labour, building (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum) + -que, and

passis: patior, patī, passus sum — to suffer, endure (perf. part. of deponent, m. dat./abl. pl.)
pectore: pectus, pectoris (n.) — breast, chest; heart (abl. sg.)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by

prius: prius (adv.) — before, sooner, earlier (nec prius… quam, not before… than)

quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than · prius… quam (conj.), before, until · indef. after sī/nē, any, some (f. acc. sg.: si quam)

quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.)

quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.)
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedesque: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sorte: sors, sortis (f.) — lot; allotment, portion, fate (abl. sg.)
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
talis: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs)
tenens: teneō, tenēre, tenuī — to hold (pres. part., nom. sg.)

tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
uno: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (m./n. abl. sg.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
utque: ut (conj.) — that, so that, as, when (+ -que 'and')
victis: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — to conquer (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. pl.)
